leftEvidence.title: Foreign residence, affliction, judgment, and departure are named beforehand

points.label: Sequence
points.left: Foreign residence and affliction are followed by judgment and coming out with possessions.
points.right: Midnight death is followed by summons, urgency, possessions received, and departure.

points.label: Time language
points.left: The promise names four hundred years of affliction and a return in the fourth generation.
points.right: The departure account states four hundred thirty years of residence and marks the departure to the day.

points.label: Movement and destination
points.left: The descendants are said to come out and later return to the land where Abram stands.
points.right: Israel begins the movement out of Egypt by traveling from Rameses to Succoth.

payload.posture: Hold the earlier promise beside the night of departure and attend to sequence, time language, judgment, possessions, and movement.

rightEvidence.title: Israel leaves Egypt after judgment, urgency, and the transfer of possessions

payload.tension: Genesis names four hundred years of affliction; Exodus states four hundred thirty years of residence and marks the departure to the day.
payload.title: Promise given / departure narrated
